title: Arizona fugitive arrested at LEGOLAND after violent attack
text:
Police say they found Jason Marchesano at LEGOLAND in California, following a community tip(Image: 2021 Daniel Knighton)

An Arizona man who was on the run following an alleged violent attack on his girlfriend, was arrested at LEGOLAND in California.

Authorities announced the arrest of Jason Marchesano, 46, on Monday. They alleged that the Arizona native used bedsheets to strangle his girlfriend, following an argument on October 28, 2025, the Yavapai County Sheriff’s Office reported.

The alleged violent attack took place in a towable recreational vehicle in the unincorporated community of Paulden, in Yavapai County. The victim managed to escape during the attack, and reported the assault. Deputies later documented bruising that matched her account of the incident, according to the sheriff’s office.

Detectives followed multiple leads in their search for Marchesano. They searched in Arizona and Nevada before learning that Marchesano had actually fled to California.

The detectives worked with local law enforcement to arrest him at the LEGOLAND resort and theme park in San Diego.

It is unclear what brought the runaway suspect to the popular family holiday-destination, which boasts over 60 family-friendly rides, shows, and attractions spread across multiple themed areas.

Marchesano is now facing charges of attempted second-degree homicide, kidnapping and aggravated assault. (Image: Yavapai Silent Witness)

However, the sheriff’s office confirmed that a tip from the community helped authorities locate the fugitive.

Marchesano is now facing charges of attempted second-degree homicide, kidnapping and aggravated assault. His next court appearance is scheduled for July 2 at the Central Courthouse in San Diego.

The Yavapai County Sheriff's Office said in a statement, "This arrest was made possible by strong investigative work, interagency partnership, and a community member who chose to speak up.”

The news comes shortly after a similar incident involving a Polish fugitive who was wanted for $30 million in fraud and money laundering. Marcin Pióro was arrested while taking part in military training at a US Army boot camp in Missouri, officials said.

The 45-year-old CEO of a Polish financial services company, was participating in military training at Fort Leonard Wood on May 19 when officials discovered he was wanted by Interpol, US Marshals said.

According to U.S. officials, Pióro had attempted to join the Illinois National Guard in a ploy to receive naturalization sponsorship.
